title: Tenant configuration fabrics for VPC customization and safe upgrades
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Customers deploying Redwood Private into customer VPCs require a predictable, minimal-surface way to apply tenant-specific customizations (networking, routing, optional managed services bindings) without forking core modules. Current approaches (per-customer forks, ad-hoc patches) create upgrade friction and increase operational burden during runtime upgrades and security patches.

Goal: Design and deliver a composable 'configuration fabric' pattern for customer Terraform repositories that: (1) lets customers declaratively express local overrides and optional components, (2) isolates per-tenant variables and secrets from upstream modules, (3) supports safe automated module upgrades with preflight checks and canary promotion, and (4) wires tenant-level health checks into Redwood Console telemetry for faster incident detection.

This ticket captures the design, implementation plan, CI/upgrade automation, and the initial rollout for 2 pilot customers.
acceptance_criteria: A composable module pattern documented and published to the internal IaC patterns repo with examples for: overlay files, variable bindings, and optional resource shims.

A reference customer repo (git) that uses the fabric pattern to apply three common customizations: custom route tables, private ECR integration, and extra IAM roles, without modifying upstream module source.
Upgrade pipeline can run a dry-run (plan) against the reference customer repo and emit a preflight report with actionable failures/warnings.
Canary upgrade flow implemented: ability to upgrade a single tenant stack and run healthchecks before promoting cluster-wide.
Automated post-upgrade healthchecks succeed and results are surfaced into Console as a per-tenant health signal.
Security review completed and acceptance from Secure Infra on variable scoping and secret handling (KMS/HSM pattern).
technical_notes: Pattern: upstream modules remain immutable; expose well-scoped input maps and feature flags. Customer repo composes a small 'fabric' module which calls upstream modules with tenant-bound inputs and injects overlay shims for optional resources.

Overlay strategy: support three overlay mechanisms in order of preference: (1) variables + feature flags, (2) optional child modules loaded via 'count' or 'for_each' controlled by inputs, (3) lightweight local-shim modules placed in /overlays that wrap or extend upstream resources (namespaced to tenant).

Upgrade safety: pipeline will execute 'terraform plan' in a controlled environment (isolated state backend with read-only snapshot) and run a terratest-driven smoke suite against canary and baseline environments.

Healthchecks: define a reusable terraform resource 'redwood_tenant_healthcheck' that registers expected endpoints / metrics into Console via an API call after apply. Healthcheck assertions implemented as small Go test binary run in CI.

Secrets: require customer secrets to be provided via remote secret backends (SOPS or KMS) referenced by data sources; do not allow inline plaintext secrets in overlay files. Pattern documented and enforced by a pre-apply lint step.
Drift detection: add a scheduled job that runs 'terraform plan' monthly on customer repos and raises drift alerts to the tenant owner if diffs are present.

CI: GitHub Actions template created for customer repos that performs: fmt/lint, plan-without-state, apply (manual), post-apply smoke tests, and registers healthcheck results. Pipeline artifacts include a machine-readable preflight_report.json.
State backend: recommend per-tenant remote state in a dedicated bucket with strict IAM roles. Provide helper module to bootstrap backend gating policies.
Observability: healthcheck failures and upgrade plan warnings will be sent to a per-tenant Slack channel via a centralized alert bridge for pilot customers.
decision_log: 2025-02-19: Chose fabric/composition pattern over forking to limit divergence and simplify upgrades (decision by @Maya, @Omar, @Priya).
2025-02-22: Standardized on three overlay mechanisms; documented priority order and recommended usage (no inline patches in upstream modules).
2025-02-25: Agreed to require remote secret backends for all pilot tenants; local secrets only allowed for PoC with explicit approval.
2025-03-01: Canary upgrade approach accepted: single-tenant apply + 24h automated smoke + manual sign-off for wider rollout.
implementation_steps: Write RFC and pattern doc in Confluence: /confluence/private/vpc/config-fabric (draft by 2025-02-21).
Create reference customer repo: github.com/redwood-inference/iac-tenant-fabric-reference (seeded with three overlays).
Author terraform helper module: redwood/tenant-fabric (semver v0.1.0) with inputs, overlay loader, and backend bootstrap.
Build GitHub Actions templates and terratest suite; add preflight_report generator.
Integrate healthcheck registration into Console API (small endpoint + auth token rotation); coordinate with Console team for telemetry mapping.
Run pilot with Customer A (EU) and Customer B (US) using the pattern; collect upgrade telemetry and iterate.
Finish security review and documentation; publish pattern in IaC patterns repo and internal playbook.
review_feedback: PM (Liam): emphasize backward-compatibility for existing customer repos; include migration steps in doc.
Design (Sofia): add diagrams showing call-graph of modules and where overlays are applied; include sequence diagram for canary upgrade.
Security (Priya): add gating policy for secrets and require KMS key usage; we should block apply if secrets are inline.
Infra (Ravi): recommend an opt-in staging account to run preflight applies to avoid noisy runs in customer production during plan checks.
qa_checks: Run terratest smoke suite against canary tenant; zero failing tests required for promotion.
Validate preflight_report contains no 'dangerous' resource deletions flagged for production state.
Run lint that enforces overlay naming and disallows inline secret literals.
Manual verification: Confirm Console shows tenant health status post-apply for pilot tenants.
